OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH & SAFETY

Protecting People.
Strengthening Operations.

Health and safety expertise for mining environments where conditions shift by the hour and definitive care is a long way from the pit.

Illustrative photography · See photography credits

OUR POSITION

A mine is only as
strong as the people
who work it.

Production targets, equipment and geology all matter. None of them hold if the workforce is exposed to harm that could have been measured, understood and controlled. Global Mino approaches occupational health and safety as technical work — evidence first, controls that match the actual hazard, and monitoring that keeps pace with a changing site.

WHAT WE DO

Six disciplines.
One duty of care.

01

Occupational Health Services

Worker health support shaped around remote mining environments — pre-placement and periodic assessment, fitness-for-task review and ongoing clinical coordination.

02

Health Risk Assessments

Systematic identification of health hazards across an operation — dust, noise, vibration, chemical agents, heat and fatigue — ranked by likelihood and consequence.

03

Health Surveillance

Structured, repeated monitoring that detects early change in worker health, so exposure controls can be corrected while the harm is still reversible.

04

Industrial Hygiene

Measurement and control of workplace exposure: respirable dust and silica, noise, ventilation, chemical agents and thermal stress.

05

Emergency Preparedness

Response planning for sites far from definitive care — scenario development, evacuation routing, drills and coordination with regional facilities.

06

Dynamic Risk Management

Risk treated as a live picture that shifts with ground conditions, weather, equipment and crew, not a document filed once and left alone.

IN THE FIELD

Controls that survive
contact with the site.

A control only works if it holds under real conditions — in heat, in dust, at the end of a long shift, on ground that has changed since the last survey. Assessment therefore happens where the work happens, not only on paper.

That fieldwork feeds back into the risk picture continuously, so exposure limits, protective equipment and emergency routes reflect the site as it is today rather than as it was when the plan was written.

OUR APPROACH

From assessment
to assurance.
